task: Review every supplied part, discover the most consequential events from the supplied evidence, cluster related reports, assign the best-fit broad news category dynamically and produce up to 150 processed stories using schema/processed-news.schema.json. The final portfolio must contain at least five well-supported stories in every category. Treat social attention as a discovery signal rather than verification. More than half of the final stories must originate with independent, local or social discovery, using the first source in each story as the discovery source; established outlets may account for no more than half.

items.title: Doesn't deserve to be public prosecutor: Supreme Court on TN law officer who withheld key evidence
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday sought the Tamil Nadu government’s response to strong remarks made by the Madras High Court against a public prosecutor who failed to place crucial evidence before the trial court in a rape case. A bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta issued notice on a challenge by the public prosecutor against the observations made by the High Court in its order. However, while doing so, it questioned the prosecutor's credibility for failing to produce an accident register before the trial court despite the register being part of his case diary. The register contained details of the injuries suffered by the rape victim. "He does not deserve to be a public prosecutor. Such a vital document you withheld. It was available in your case diary. May be technically you may be right that no notice was given but you don't deserve any notice, as a matter of fact. You don't deserve to be a public prosecutor." the Court said. items.title: MP/MLA endorsement for women to get ₹2,500 financial assistance a policy decision, did not "come out of sky: Delhi govt to HC
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Monday said that it could declare the Delhi Lakshmi Yojana arbitrary if even one deserving woman is excluded from the scheme because of lack of endorsement from the local Member of the Legislative Assembly (MLA) or the Member of Parliament (MP). Under the Delhi Lakshmi Yojana, the Delhi government provides financial assistance of ₹2,500 per month to eligible women. A Division Bench of Chief Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya and Justice Tejas Karia today questioned the rationale behind the condition requiring MP or MLA endorsement. “What is the objective you are trying to achieve by this? Suppose you don’t know any MP or MLA? If even one person is left out [because of the condition], then the scheme is arbitrary. What is the objective you are trying to achieve through this condition? There are thousands of ways you can identify people,” the Bench remarked. Delhi High Court If even one person is left out [because of the condition], then the scheme is arbitrary. Ameer-Ul-Islam is the sole convict sentenced to death for the 2016 rape and murder of a Dalit law student in Kerala's Perumbavoor. A Bench of Justice Dipankar Datta and Justice Sheel Nagu was hearing his plea seeking his transfer from Viyyur Central Prison in Kerala to a jail in Assam, where his wife and aged parents reside. She submitted that a prisoner sentenced to death cannot ordinarily be transferred without special permission from the government, except in circumstances where the prisoner's presence is required before a court. John submitted that the proceedings referred to in the provision had already concluded, pointing out that the Kerala High Court had confirmed the death sentence. items.title: Mockery of Supreme Court order: Karnataka High Court directs State wide audit of CCTV in police stations
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court recently took strong exception to the State government's argument that CCTV cameras at a police station in Bengaluru were not working due to power outage and lack of back up power [V Shailaja v The Commissioner] . Justice Suraj Govindaraj said that such a stance amounted to mockery of the Supreme Court' s 2020 order to install CCTV cameras in all police stations. "Mockery of the Supreme Court order..What to do? This is a mockery of the order and you submit a report that you complied (with the Supreme Court order). There's an affidavit filed in Supreme Court that every police station has CCTV cameras, fully functional 24 hours. The only conclusion we can arrive at is that you were also happy with it not working; that is why you did not do anything for 1.5 years, it served your purpose. There is no other conclusion that we can draw," the Court remarked. The very purpose of installing CCTV cameras in police stations is defeated if the systems are allowed to remain non-functional during power outages, the bench said. items.title: Jammu & Kashmir HC seeks senior AAG’s assistance on applicability of BNSS to pre-2024 defamation case

Vinus Sharma ]. Justice Wasim Sadiq Nargal on August 3, sought the assistance of a Senior Additional Advocate General in the matter. The case involves a question of whether the Bhartiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023 - which replaced the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (CrPC) with effect from July 1, 2024 - would be applicable to a criminal complaint arising from an offence committed before the new criminal laws came into force. “ Since an important question of law has been raised in the instant matter, this Court, in the peculiar facts and circumstances of the case, deems it appropriate to request Ms. Monika Kohli, learned Senior AAG, to render valuable assistance in the instant matter with a view to appreciate the controversy in question," the High Court said. items.summary: The tiger has a place both in the artwork of India’s original Constitution and in maintaining the country’s ecological balance, Union Minister of State for Law and Justice (Independent Charge) Arjun Ram Meghwal said on Saturday. Meghwal was speaking at the launch of Sacred Tiger Tales: From Vedic Hymns to Tryst with Stripes , authored and photographed by senior Law Ministry official Manoj Kumar. The 248-page coffee-table book, published by OakBridge Publishing, was unveiled by Meghwal alongside Attorney Genera l R Venkataramani at the India International Centre in New Delhi. The book features 82 short narratives spanning scripture, classical literature, folklore, colonial history, and modern conservation, alongside photographs taken across Indian tiger reserves. The launch brought together figures across law, government, wildlife conservation, photography and publishing. items.title: As Kerala mulls Muvattupuzha district, IUML renews demand to split Malappuram
items.summary: Follow TNM's WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. The demand to bifurcate Kerala’s Malappuram district has gained renewed momentum, with Indian Union Muslim League (IUML) leader and Tanur MLA PK Navas calling for the creation of a new district to improve administrative efficiency. The demand, which has been around for decades, has resurfaced after the Kerala government announced plans to examine the possibility of splitting Ernakulam district and creating a new district centred around Muvattupuzha. Kerala Chief Minister V D Satheesan had earlier announced that the state would constitute a Delimitation Commission to examine the proposal for a new Muvattupuzha district. In a Facebook post, Navas said the same rationale should apply to Malappuram, which he said has a greater administrative burden because of its population and geographical spread. “With a population of 41.13 lakh, an area of 3,550 square kilometres, and a population density of 1,157 people per square kilometre, the demand for a new district in Malappuram is also well justified (2011 Census),” Navas said.
